lastText: File ClosedThe Coup That Didn't TakeContestedItalian High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: SEPTEMBER 1943: SPECULATIVEImmediate AftermathThis file closes on September 1943, a speculative branch's own ending rather than a date the ██████████ record recognizes: six weeks of an Italian army fighting itself that the actual, bloodless transition of July 1943 █████ had to spend. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined █████ ██████ two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. The Mediterranean question was answered with an actual 1940 invasion of Malta, while the garrison was still weak: the operation the historical Comando Supremo only ever planned as Operation Hercules a year too late, attempted, won, and then held against Britain's own attempt to take it back. A speculative path with almost no historical footing: the officer corps' ██████ loyalty to the constitutional monarchy in July 1943 proved deeper than any loyalty to Mussolini personally. What this file records instead is a counterfactual crisis of legitimacy inside the regime's own institutions: one the losing war underneath it would have overtaken regardless of who signed the orders.
